$comment: Breakthrough scores for the /math wall: for each openai/math family, how big a breakthrough it would be IF THE CLAIM HOLDS. Dimensions and anchors live in lib/math-breakthrough.ts (importance 0-4, advance 0-4, consequences 0-4, surprise 0-3; confidence 0-3 is recorded separately and never enters the score). `why` (<=140 chars) says what was claimed; `consequence` (<=200 chars) says what would improve, and for whom. Scored by hand from catalogue-data.ts, data/math-wall/notes.json, the openai-math article and the release repo, batch by discipline. Checked by `pnpm validate:breakthrough`.

001.why: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for Hodge classes mod p; the strongest form leans on the release's unchecked Hodge paper.
001.consequence: A working theory of rational Tate classes on abelian varieties mod p, which Langlands–Rapoport style questions need. Internal to arithmetic geometry.

002.why: The exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula for curves of rank 0 or 1, prime by prime; 340 unchecked pages chained to other release papers.
002.consequence: For every elliptic curve with Selmer corank 0 or 1, Sha's size and the L-value become theorems, not predictions. Feeds the release's Hilbert-tenth proof.

003.why: Rules out zeta and Dirichlet L-function zeros right of 7/8: the first zero-free half-plane ever; Lean checks it against mathlib's zeta.
003.consequence: Prime counts in progressions get error terms of x^{7/8} without assumptions, so results now proved only under GRH-type hypotheses could become unconditional.

004.why: Shows no algorithm can decide if a polynomial equation has rational solutions; rests on three other unchecked release papers.
004.consequence: Closes the decidability question over Q that followed Matiyasevich. Nothing practical changes: the answer is that no algorithm exists.

005.why: Proves Catalan's constant is irrational, a long-open question, with a new determinant method; Lean checks the main theorem.
005.consequence: A first irrationality proof for Catalan's constant; its determinant method is what the release's π result is built on.

006.why: Half of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve have rank 0 and half rank 1, as Goldfeld predicted in 1979; long and unformalized.
006.consequence: The average rank of quadratic twists becomes 1/2, unconditionally. It feeds the release's BSD and Hilbert-tenth families, so an error would spread.

007.why: Two-point Chowla with ordinary averages: n and n+h have uncorrelated prime-factor parity; more points stay open. Lean checks it.
007.consequence: Better control of sign patterns of the Liouville function at a single scale. Mostly internal to analytic number theory.

008.why: Proves the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture that the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is free; Lean checks the main theorem.
008.consequence: Pins down the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with consequences for Kontsevich's graph complex and deformation quantization.

009.why: Bogomolov's program: a function field is rebuilt from a tiny piece of its Galois data; Lean checks only the easy direction.
009.consequence: Tiny Galois data is enough to rebuild a function field. Internal to anabelian geometry.

010.why: Odd 2-dimensional Galois representations at the awkward prime 2 come from modular forms; 113 unformalized pages.
010.consequence: Removes the p=2 gap in Fontaine–Mazur for odd 2-dimensional representations, and supplies modularity input to the release's Hilbert-tenth proof.

011.why: Prime factors of p−1 follow the random-integer law; needs primes in progressions past a classic barrier. Unformalized.
011.consequence: Gives the totient-fibre conjecture (via Erdős–Pomerance) and strong counts of smooth shifted primes, by passing a known level-of-distribution barrier.

012.why: Whether n is smooth tells you nothing about n+1: the joint Dickman law with ordinary density. Lean checks it.
012.consequence: Settles whether smoothness of n and n+1 are independent. Little follow-on outside analytic number theory.

013.why: The primes are not a sumset A+B, settling Ostmann's inverse Goldbach question; Lean checks the full statement.
013.consequence: Closes Ostmann's question about the primes as a sumset. Little follow-on expected.

014.why: Restricted geometric Langlands in characteristic p, with Ramanujan bounds as a consequence; 348 pages, conditions on p, no Lean.
014.consequence: Ties function-field automorphic forms to geometry in characteristic p and yields Ramanujan bounds for generic cusp forms; inputs for the Langlands program.

015.why: Higher-degree analogue of Duke's equidistribution theorem in prime, quartic and sextic degree; Lean covers prime degree.
015.consequence: Extends equidistribution of torus orbits to higher-degree number fields. Internal to homogeneous dynamics.

016.why: Zilber–Pink unlikely intersections for abelian varieties over algebraic numbers; non-effective and unformalized.
016.consequence: Finiteness of unlikely intersections in abelian varieties, the setting that unifies Manin–Mumford and Mordell–Lang. Non-effective, so no explicit bounds.

017.why: Pins π's irrationality exponent at exactly 2, after 70 years moved the bound only from 42 to 7.1; Lean checks the statement.
017.consequence: Settles how well π can be approximated by fractions. No computation changes; the method may extend to other constants.

018.why: Finishes the last exceptional cases of the Margulis–Platonov conjecture on normal subgroups of arithmetic groups. No Lean.
018.consequence: Completes the description of normal subgroups of arithmetic groups, an input to the congruence subgroup problem.

019.why: The p-adic section conjecture: rational points are exactly the Galois sections; 31 pages for a famous problem, unformalized.
019.consequence: Rational points of p-adic curves can be read off from Galois sections; the global conjecture follows only for specific modular curves.

020.why: Values like n^4+2 are squarefree a positive share of the time, and higher powers likewise; Lean checks every degree.
020.consequence: Positive-proportion squarefree values for quartics and power-free values in every degree. Internal to sieve theory.

021.why: Brings Jacobsthal's function down to about k squared; the true size is still open. Lean checks the bound.
021.consequence: Better worst-case bounds for runs of sieved integers; the true order stays open.

022.why: The shifted, weak form of the Duffin–Schaeffer approximation theorem; the coprime form stays open. Unformalized.
022.consequence: Extends Duffin–Schaeffer approximation theory to shifted targets. Internal to Diophantine approximation.

023.why: Patterson's bias for cubic Gauss sums at primes, without assuming GRH; Lean checks the main theorem.
023.consequence: Removes GRH from Patterson's prediction for cubic Gauss sums. Internal to analytic number theory.

024.why: An asymptotic count of Euler-phi values up to x, with an oscillating factor rather than a constant; Lean checks it.
024.consequence: A sharper count of the values of Euler's function. Nothing follows beyond itself.

025.why: Every fraction a/b is a sum of about log log b distinct unit fractions, as Erdős conjectured; Lean checks it.
025.consequence: The worst case for Egyptian-fraction length is now known. Closes a gap with little follow-on.

026.why: A fixed share of prime gaps exceed C times the average gap, for every C, without conjectures; Lean checks a corollary.
026.consequence: Confirms a random-model prediction about large prime gaps without conjectures; the constants are tiny.

027.why: Integral points on surface-group character varieties are dense after one field extension; 27 unformalized pages.
027.consequence: Integer points on character varieties are dense, which bears on which local systems come from geometry. Internal.

028.why: The Gaussian moat problem: bounded steps on Gaussian primes never reach infinity. Short sieve proof; Lean checks it.
028.consequence: Answers the Gaussian moat puzzle. The proof is really about sieved lattices; nothing follows beyond it.

029.why: Every admissible base is a primitive root mod infinitely many primes, via a huge unproved-elsewhere zero-free strip. No Lean.
029.consequence: The qualitative Artin conjecture for every base; its zero-free strip would also give deterministic polynomial factoring (family 142).

030.why: Every elliptic curve over an imaginary quadratic field is modular; 30 pages for a statement that needed ten authors before.
030.consequence: Lets the L-function methods used for curves over Q apply to elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields.

031.why: Uchida's question: open maps between Galois groups of number fields come from field embeddings. Unformalized.
031.consequence: Strengthens the reconstruction of number fields from Galois groups. Internal to anabelian geometry.

032.why: The Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and K3 products, the classic test case; made outside the usual procedure, no Lean.
032.consequence: Algebraic cycles for every Hodge class on CM abelian varieties and K3 products; feeds Milne's rationality question and Tate-class theory (family 001).

033.why: Iitaka's 1970s subadditivity conjecture, a backbone of classifying varieties; Lean checks only a small side case.
033.consequence: Kodaira dimension adds up correctly in fibrations, a key input to the abundance and minimal-model results in this release.

034.why: Log abundance, the last big gap in the minimal model program, but assuming a subadditivity statement; 781 unchecked pages.
034.consequence: Would complete the abundance step of the minimal model program (conditionally); much of the classification of varieties rests on it.

035.why: One numerical case of threefold abundance in characteristic p above 3; a single case of a larger program. No Lean.
035.consequence: One more case of abundance in characteristic p. Little follow-on.

036.why: Minimal models exist for generalized pairs; stands or falls with the release's own unchecked abundance and termination papers.
036.consequence: Minimal models for generalized pairs, the form that induction in birational geometry actually needs.

037.why: The next-largest singularity volume after smooth points is the ordinary double point, in every dimension; no Lean.
037.consequence: Bounds the volume of singular K-semistable Fano varieties. Internal to K-stability.

038.why: Fujita's freeness conjecture: K plus n+1 copies of an ample bundle is base-point free; 25 unchecked pages.
038.consequence: Effective global generation of adjoint bundles in every dimension, a standard tool for building maps; used here for Kobayashi's conjecture.

039.why: Nagata's 1959 conjecture on plane curves through very general points; Lean states and checks the full conjecture.
039.consequence: Fixes the nef cone of the plane blown up at very general points and the maximal Seshadri constants, which the SHGH line of work waited on.

040.why: Bloch's conjecture: surfaces without 2-forms have trivial zero-cycles; the fake-projective-plane case needs scrutiny.
040.consequence: Zero-cycles on surfaces without 2-forms are trivial, closing a central case of the Bloch–Beilinson picture for surfaces.

041.why: Every hyperkähler manifold with a square-zero nef class is a Lagrangian torus fibration over projective space. No Lean.
041.consequence: Such hyperkähler manifolds fiber over projective space, which matters for their classification and for SYZ mirror symmetry.

042.why: K3 surfaces are Oka (maps into them are as flexible as into C^n); the broader title over-reaches the paper. No Lean.
042.consequence: Adds K3 surfaces to the list of Oka manifolds. Internal to complex analysis.

043.why: Extends the recently proved P=W for GL_n to fixed-determinant SL_n moduli; builds on the known proofs. No Lean.
043.consequence: Extends P=W to SL_n. Internal to nonabelian Hodge theory.

044.why: An equivariant form of Hikita's symplectic-duality conjecture, under a regular stability assumption. No Lean.
044.consequence: Confirms a symplectic-duality prediction in a regular setting. Internal to geometric representation theory.

046.why: Disproves Shafarevich's holomorphic-convexity conjecture with a surface and a fourfold; a short disproof that needs checking.
046.consequence: Ends hopes that universal covers are always holomorphically convex; the release's abelianity result builds on it.

047.why: A 4-dimensional counterexample to Zariski cancellation over C, open 50 years; Lean checks both halves. Dimension 3 stays open.
047.consequence: Cancellation fails over C in dimension 4; dimension 3 remains. Internal to affine geometry.

048.why: A singular surface with free tangent sheaf disproves the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic 0. No Lean.
048.consequence: Free vector fields do not force smoothness. Internal to singularity theory.

049.why: A polynomial in 4 variables whose zero set is flat space yet is not a coordinate, refuting Abhyankar–Sathaye; Lean checks it.
049.consequence: The embedding conjecture fails from dimension 4 on. Internal to affine algebraic geometry.

050.why: Ampleness does not imply a positively curved metric: a counterexample to Griffiths' 1969 conjecture. Lean uses custom definitions.
050.consequence: Separates algebraic and metric positivity of vector bundles, redirecting work on Griffiths positivity.

051.why: Kobayashi's conjecture that hyperbolic manifolds have ample canonical bundle; downstream of the least-checked release papers.
051.consequence: Links hyperbolicity to an ample canonical bundle, settling a central question in complex hyperbolicity.

052.why: A two-factor, integrable case of Beauville's splitting conjecture for Kähler manifolds; Lean checks it on custom foundations.
052.consequence: One case of Beauville's splitting conjecture. Internal.

053.why: Pixton's relations do not give all tautological relations in Chow; the example lives in genus around 10^60. No Lean.
053.consequence: Pixton's relations must be extended to describe Chow rings of moduli of curves. Internal.

054.why: Cubic fourfolds with a geometric K3 category yet irrational, refuting Kuznetsov's rationality prediction; unformalized.
054.consequence: Rules out the categorical criterion for rationality of cubic fourfolds that the field had been pursuing.

055.why: Bridgeland stability near large volume on Calabi–Yau threefolds via a corrected Bogomolov-type inequality. No Lean.
055.consequence: Stability conditions on Calabi–Yau threefolds near large volume, which physics predicts and enumerative geometry uses.

056.why: Every sequence of flips stops on fourfolds, projective and Kähler; termination stays open in dimension 5 and up. No Lean.
056.consequence: Flips terminate in dimension four, completing the minimal model program there.

057.why: Campana's special varieties have virtually abelian fundamental groups, via L2 Hodge theory; unformalized.
057.consequence: Campana's prediction that special varieties have virtually abelian fundamental groups; used by families 058 and 051.

058.why: Kollár–Pardon's classification of semialgebraic universal covers; Lean checks only the bounded-domain half.
058.consequence: Classifies which universal covers are semialgebraic. Internal.

059.why: High-dimensional singularities with the same topology but different multiplicity, answering Zariski; surfaces stay open.
059.consequence: Topology alone does not fix multiplicity in high dimension; the surface case stays open. Internal.

060.why: Every class VII surface with b2>0 has a global spherical shell, completing their classification; 39 unchecked pages.
060.consequence: Completes the classification of minimal class VII surfaces with b2>0, the last unclassified compact complex surfaces.

062.why: LeBrun–Salamon: every contact Fano manifold is homogeneous, a long-standing conjecture with only partial cases before.
062.consequence: Classifies contact Fano manifolds and, through twistor spaces, positive quaternion-Kähler manifolds.

063.why: The generalized Mukai bound on Picard number of Fano manifolds, by a short Gromov–Witten argument; unrefereed, no Lean.
063.consequence: A sharp Picard-number bound for Fano manifolds. Internal.

064.why: Constant Milnor number implies constant topology for surface singularities, the case Lê–Ramanujam left open. No Lean.
064.consequence: Closes the last case of the Lê–Ramanujam problem. Internal.

065.why: Virasoro constraints for Gromov–Witten invariants of complete intersections, beyond semisimple targets. No Lean.
065.consequence: Virasoro constraints for more target spaces. Internal to Gromov–Witten theory.

066.why: Bounded-index klt complements for Fano contractions, a finiteness tool for boundedness of Fanos. No Lean.
066.consequence: A finiteness tool behind boundedness results for Fano varieties.

067.why: Adds dimension six to the Campana–Peternell conjecture on Fano manifolds with nef tangent bundle; one more dimension.
067.consequence: One more dimension of a conjecture. Nothing follows beyond it.

068.why: Manifolds with semipositive anticanonical bundle have a pluri-anticanonical section, over a seven-paper chain. No Lean.
068.consequence: Nonvanishing for anticanonical bundles under curvature assumptions. Internal.

069.why: Quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level; rational and critical levels are excluded. No Lean.
069.consequence: Quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level. Internal to geometric representation theory.

071.why: Koebe's 1908 question: domains with infinitely many holes can be mapped to circle domains; Lean states and checks it.
071.consequence: Circle-domain models exist for wild domains; uniqueness stays open. Internal to complex analysis.

072.why: Brennan's conjecture on conformal maps, stuck for 25 years, plus a refuted 1996 formula; Lean checks the main theorem.
072.consequence: Sharp area-distortion bounds for conformal maps and a settled value of the integral-means spectrum.

073.why: Falconer's distance conjecture: big fractals have a positive-length set of distances, in every dimension; Lean checks it.
073.consequence: Settles geometric measure theory's central distance question with a multiscale method others can reuse.

074.why: Kakeya: the maximal estimate in 3D and the set conjecture in 4D, one dimension past Wang–Zahl; long and unformalized.
074.consequence: Kakeya bounds drive restriction, Bochner–Riesz and PDE estimates; the 4D set result is the next step toward the full conjecture.

075.why: Fourier series of L log L functions converge almost everywhere, the conjectured edge past Carleson, by an entropy method. No Lean.
075.consequence: Fixes where Fourier series stop converging almost everywhere. Internal to harmonic analysis.

076.why: Plus/minus-one polynomials can be ultraflat and merit factors unbounded, against Erdős's guess; Lean checks the upper half.
076.consequence: Answers coding theory's question on the merit factor of binary sequences, and Littlewood's flatness question.

077.why: The Fourier restriction conjecture for positively curved surfaces in 3D, leaning on the release's own Kakeya paper. No Lean.
077.consequence: Restriction estimates feed PDE, number theory and Bochner–Riesz; this would settle the positively curved case in 3D.

078.why: The Bochner–Riesz conjecture in three dimensions by an entropy transport scheme; 114 unformalized pages.
078.consequence: Sharp Fourier summation in 3D, implying restriction for the sphere.

079.why: Sharp local smoothing for waves in 3+1 dimensions, which would imply 3D Bochner–Riesz, restriction and Kakeya. No Lean.
079.consequence: One estimate implying 3D Bochner–Riesz, restriction and Kakeya maximal bounds, plus sharp regularity for wave equations.

080.why: The exact endpoint of Carleson's Schrödinger convergence problem; the sharp range up to it was already known. No Lean.
080.consequence: Closes the endpoint of Carleson's Schrödinger problem. Little follow-on.

081.why: The David–Semmes problem in higher codimension: bounded Riesz transforms force rectifiable sets; Lean checks it.
081.consequence: Characterizes rectifiable sets by Riesz transforms in every codimension, a tool in geometric measure theory.

082.why: The first bound of any kind for the triangular Hilbert transform, at its symmetric point; a new trace method, Lean-checked.
082.consequence: A first bound for an entangled singular integral; its trace-energy method may reach other multilinear forms.

083.why: Stein's conjecture: Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz direction fields are bounded at short scales; Lean checks it.
083.consequence: Settles Stein's Lipschitz conjecture; the Zygmund differentiation problem stays open.

084.why: Erdős's similarity conjecture for geometric sequences like 1/2, 1/4, 1/8; the general case stays open. Lean covers ratio 1/2.
084.consequence: Resolves Erdős similarity for geometric sequences. Internal.

085.why: In the plane, centered disk averages do not increase gradient variation; one case of a Hajłasz–Onninen question.
085.consequence: One case of a regularity question for maximal functions. Nothing follows beyond it.

086.why: A first L^p bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform, at one exponent; 93 pages written a day before release. No Lean.
086.consequence: Would open the multilinear Hilbert transform hierarchy, and feeds the release's pointwise ergodic result (family 154).

087.why: Mahler's 1939 volume-product conjecture for symmetric bodies, via a symplectic ball, with two proofs; Lean checks it.
087.consequence: Sharp volume-product bound for symmetric convex bodies, with a new link to symplectic capacities.

088.why: Petty's projection inequality in dimension 4 and up; dimension 3 relies on separate human work. Lean checks it.
088.consequence: A sharp affine isoperimetric inequality. Internal to convex geometry.

089.why: Planar and bounded-treewidth graphs embed in L1 with bounded distortion, a 25-year-old cut question; Lean checks it.
089.consequence: Bounded flow-cut gaps on planar and bounded-treewidth networks: sparsest-cut relaxations are constant-factor there.

090.why: The hexagonal lattice minimizes energy for every completely monotone interaction (Cohn–Kumar in 2D); Lean checks the core.
090.consequence: Explains why hexagonal patterns minimize energy in 2D systems such as vortices and Coulomb gases; sharp packing certificates.

091.why: The log Brunn–Minkowski inequality for symmetric bodies, plus the B-conjecture, in 20 pages; Lean checks the main theorem.
091.consequence: Uniqueness for the logarithmic Minkowski problem and the B-conjecture follow.

092.why: One lattice covers space with density of order n log n, and some bodies need that much; sharpens very recent work.
092.consequence: Pins the worst case of covering density. Internal.

093.why: Subgaussian log-concave measures satisfy a dimension-free log-Sobolev inequality, answering a 2023 question. No Lean.
093.consequence: Gaussian concentration for subgaussian log-concave measures. Internal to high-dimensional probability.

094.why: n points in L_p fit in n^{o(1)} dimensions at fixed distortion, a Johnson–Lindenstrauss analogue; Lean checks it.
094.consequence: Dimension reduction for L_p data, once thought to need near-linear dimension; constants are not worked out.

095.why: Hyperbolicity cones that are not slices of PSD cones, refuting the generalized Lax conjecture; Lean checks the weaker form.
095.consequence: Hyperbolic programming is strictly more expressive than semidefinite programming, an optimization theory question.

096.why: Khot–Naor's propeller conjecture on Gaussian partitions in every dimension; Lean checks the full statement.
096.consequence: Fixes the approximability of kernel clustering, conditional on the release's Unique Games proof.

097.why: Unit vectors summing to zero can be ordered so partial sums stay within about √d; Lean checks the bound.
097.consequence: A sharp vector-balancing bound, without an efficient algorithm.

098.why: A doubling subset of Hilbert space with no bi-Lipschitz copy in any R^k, the famous open case; 13 Lean-checked pages.
098.consequence: Settles the Hilbert-space case of dimension reduction for doubling sets, negatively.

099.why: Edit distance embeds into L1 no better than Ostrovsky–Rabani's 2005 scheme, up to the exponent's constant; Lean checks it.
099.consequence: Edit distance cannot be embedded into L1 much better than known, closing a line in nearest-neighbour search theory.

100.why: Cylinders can cover a tetrahedron with slightly under half its shadow area; the saving is about 5e-10. Lean checks it.
100.consequence: Moves the best constant in a covering inequality by about 5e-10. Nothing follows beyond it.

101.why: Simplices have the largest isotropic constant; if right it also gives the non-symmetric Mahler conjecture. No Lean.
101.consequence: Settles which convex bodies have the largest isotropic constant and, if right, the non-symmetric Mahler conjecture.

102.why: The Unique Games Conjecture: the simple SDP algorithms for Max-Cut and Vertex Cover are optimal unless P=NP. Lean checks it.
102.consequence: Exact approximation limits for Max-Cut, Vertex Cover and every CSP: decades of results conditional on UGC become conditional only on P≠NP.

103.why: Coins never help small-memory computation (L = BPL), the space analogue of P = BPP; one 108-page manuscript, no Lean.
103.consequence: Randomness never saves memory: every randomized log-space algorithm can be made deterministic, though the time bound may be huge.

104.why: Quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games; polynomial time is still open. Partial Lean.
104.consequence: Faster theoretical algorithms for games used in verification and controller synthesis; no practical change claimed.

105.why: 2-to-1 games are hard even with perfect completeness, Khot's strongest d-to-1 form; extends a nine-day-old human result.
105.consequence: Hardness for coloring-type problems from perfect completeness, extending very recent work.

106.why: Coloring 3-colorable graphs with any fixed number of colors is NP-hard, but that part was published days earlier by others.
106.consequence: A stronger hardness result for coloring; the headline corollary was already known.

107.why: Matrix multiplication exponent ω ≤ 9/4, a bigger drop than the last 36 years combined, in 13 pages; Lean checks the bound.
107.consequence: Asymptotically faster algorithms for everything bottlenecked by matrix multiplication; non-constructive, so no practical algorithm yet.

108.why: The permanent needs determinants of cubic size, after 20 years stuck at quadratic; VP vs VNP stays open. Lean checks it.
108.consequence: The best lower bound toward VP vs VNP, though still far from separating them.

109.why: Integer multiplication slightly below n log n on multitape machines; the saving is far too small ever to matter. No Lean.
109.consequence: n log n is not the floor for multiplication on Turing machines; no practical effect.

110.why: Randomized k-server achieves the optimal log² k on every metric; existence only, no efficient algorithm. Lean checks it.
110.consequence: The optimal competitive ratio for randomized k-server on any metric, as an existence result.

111.why: With one sample per item, a constant fraction of the prophet's value on any matroid; the constant is 2^-310.
111.consequence: Constant-factor posted-price mechanisms from one sample; the constant is far too small to use.

112.why: Depth-3 circuit lower bounds past the 2^√n barrier by a growing factor in the exponent; Lean checks it.
112.consequence: The first superconstant gain past the depth-3 barrier, on a known route to bigger circuit lower bounds.

113.why: Perfect matchings in any graph can be approximately counted in polynomial time, open since 2001 for non-bipartite graphs.
113.consequence: Polynomial-time approximate counting and sampling of perfect matchings in every graph: dimer models, 0/1 hafnians.

114.why: Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids, unifying matching and log-concave methods; Lean covers two matroids.
114.consequence: Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids, unifying known samplers.

115.why: Provably fast sampling of contingency tables with any margins, the null model behind Fisher's exact test; Lean checks it.
115.consequence: A provably polynomial sampler for contingency tables, the null model behind Fisher's exact test; exponents are large.

116.why: One explicit set of matrices certifies every small noncommutative formula is nonzero, in any characteristic.
116.consequence: Black-box identity testing for noncommutative formulas. Internal to derandomization.

117.why: Uniform sparsest cut has no constant-factor algorithm unless P=NP; Lean checks only the SDP gap half.
117.consequence: The ARV algorithm is near-optimal for uniform sparsest cut, so graph partitioning has a firm approximation limit.

118.why: Bin packing's configuration LP can be off by any number of bins, refuting the conjectured one-bin gap; Lean checks it.
118.consequence: Bin packing cannot be solved within any fixed number of bins efficiently; the cutting-stock LP's gap is unbounded.

119.why: Courtade–Kumar: sending one coordinate is the best one-bit summary through a noisy channel; Lean checks the main result.
119.consequence: Settles a basic information-theory question. Little follow-on.

120.why: Maximum matching in general graphs in almost-linear time, after 45 years at m√n; Monte Carlo and unformalized.
120.consequence: Near-linear-time maximum matching in any graph, in theory; practical matching codes are unaffected for now.

121.why: Edit distance approximated to any fixed accuracy in almost-linear time; thresholds are huge. Lean checks it.
121.consequence: Near-linear (1+ε) edit distance in theory; aligners are unaffected because the thresholds are huge.

122.why: Worst-case trace reconstruction needs between n^{log log n} and quasipolynomially many traces; Lean covers the lower bound.
122.consequence: Ends hopes of polynomial worst-case trace reconstruction, a toy model for DNA storage.

124.why: Unit jobs with precedences on three machines are schedulable in polynomial time, a Garey–Johnson open problem; Lean checks it.
124.consequence: Puts a Garey–Johnson problem in P; the n^150020 algorithm is unusable.

125.why: A polynomial algorithm reaches the 1+2/e hardness floor for metric k-median, closing its approximability; Lean checks it.
125.consequence: Closes k-median's approximability with an algorithm matching the hardness floor.

126.why: No polynomial-size semidefinite program describes the matching polytope; Lean checks a weaker superpolynomial form.
126.consequence: Rules out small SDPs for matching. Internal to extension complexity.

127.why: Gotsman–Linial: degree-d threshold functions have average sensitivity O(d√n), open 30 years; 13 Lean-checked pages.
127.consequence: Agnostic learning and noise-sensitivity bounds for polynomial threshold functions.

128.why: A factor-2 algorithm for shortest common superstring, the long-sought target; the Greedy conjecture stays open.
128.consequence: A 2-approximation for superstrings; genome assemblers use different objectives.

129.why: Two-way deterministic automata need exponentially more states than nondeterministic ones: Sakoda–Sipser (1978). Lean checks it.
129.consequence: Settles descriptional complexity's flagship question, with no complexity-class consequence.

130.why: The FFT's n log n is beatable with exact complex constants, by a factor of n^(10^-13); Lean checks a weaker form.
130.consequence: The FFT is not optimal in the unrestricted model; FFTW and cuFFT are unaffected.

131.why: The edge-switch chain used to sample graphs with given degrees mixes in polynomial time for every sequence; Lean checks it.
131.consequence: Justifies the switch-chain sampling network scientists use for degree-sequence null models; the bound is too loose to set step counts.

132.why: Block sensitivity can exceed sensitivity squared, against the natural guess; an 11-page, Lean-checked construction.
132.consequence: Sharpens the sensitivity picture after Huang's theorem. Internal.

133.why: The n^k cost of k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman is unavoidable, by a diagonalization-style bound; Lean checks it.
133.consequence: Higher-order Weisfeiler–Leman, and so higher-order GNNs, cannot avoid the n^k cost. Internal.

134.why: Three nested stars suffice for any regular language with complement; whether one suffices stays open. Lean checks it.
134.consequence: Bounds generalized star height by 3; whether 1 suffices stays open.

135.why: Homogeneous depth-5 circuits for iterated matrix multiplication need size n^Θ(√n); Lean checks both bounds.
135.consequence: Sharp homogeneous depth-5 bounds. Internal to algebraic complexity.

136.why: A PCP theorem for PPAD with quasilinear blow-up, so approximate equilibria stay hard; 147 pages, no Lean.
136.consequence: Robust PPAD-hardness for approximate Nash equilibria; stronger bounds follow under ETH.

137.why: One-tape machines running time t can be simulated in space t^{2/5}, below the square-root barrier; unformalized.
137.consequence: Suggests the square root is not the space limit for simulating time; one-tape model only.

138.why: Worst-case Subset Sum in 2^{0.49n}, the first break of the 1974 meet-in-the-middle barrier, by a hair; no Lean.
138.consequence: A worst-case Subset Sum speed-up, with knock-on gains for related knapsack problems; cryptography unaffected.

139.why: Sampling log-concave distributions needs only d^ε gradient queries, though computation between queries is unbounded.
139.consequence: An information-theoretic query bound for sampling; Bayesian samplers are unaffected.

140.why: Low-memory learners pay an extra log(1/ε) factor in samples for noiseless Gaussian regression; Lean checks it.
140.consequence: A clean memory–sample tradeoff for streaming regression in a narrow setting.

141.why: Existential-universal real sentences sit in the counting hierarchy, well below PSPACE; unformalized.
141.consequence: A better upper bound for existential-universal real problems. Internal.

142.why: Deterministic polynomial factoring over prime fields, if the release's unchecked Artin paper holds; no Lean.
142.consequence: Deterministic polynomial factoring and nonresidue finding, if the release's zero-free strip holds; libraries are unaffected.

143.why: Hilbert's 16th problem: each degree has a uniform bound on limit cycles, with no number given; the Lean covers a side case only.
143.consequence: A finite limit-cycle bound for each degree of planar polynomial ODEs; with no numbers, applications must wait for estimates.

144.why: Banach's question: a measure-preserving map whose spectrum is a single Lebesgue shift; 30 pages, Lean checks it.
144.consequence: Answers a spectral-theory question. Internal to ergodic theory.

145.why: Rokhlin's 1949 problem: mixing implies mixing of all orders; 40 pages for a famous problem, and Lean checks it.
145.consequence: Mixing implies mixing of all orders; the release's pointwise ergodic results use it.

146.why: The standard map, the textbook model of chaos, has positive entropy for all large k; Lean checks the main theorem.
146.consequence: Rigorous chaos on positive area for the standard map, the textbook Hamiltonian model; no ergodicity claim.

147.why: Birkhoff billiards: a continuous collar of caustics near the boundary forces an ellipse; the full conjecture stays open.
147.consequence: A local rigidity theorem for billiards. Internal.

148.why: Self-similar measures lose dimension only through exact overlaps, settling the exact-overlaps conjecture; Lean checks it.
148.consequence: The dimension of self-similar measures is computable from entropy, settling the exact-overlaps conjecture.

149.why: Weakly reversible mass-action reaction networks keep every species bounded away from 0 and infinity; Lean checks less.
149.consequence: Weakly reversible chemical reaction networks never let a species die out or blow up, a long-standing question in that theory.

150.why: Billiards in a triangle with an irrational angle are weakly mixing; two short papers for a hard problem. Lean checks ergodicity.
150.consequence: Weak mixing for irrational triangle billiards, with claimed quantum-ergodicity corollaries.

151.why: A C1 map whose homology grows but entropy does not, against Shub's entropy conjecture; the diffeomorphism case stays open.
151.consequence: C1 smoothness is not enough to force entropy growth; the diffeomorphism case stays open.

152.why: A zero-entropy system with no smooth volume-preserving model, so entropy is not the only obstruction; Lean checks less.
152.consequence: A new obstruction to smooth realization of abstract systems. Internal.

153.why: A first non-Pisot singular Bernoulli convolution, at quartic Salem numbers, against a long expectation; unformalized.
153.consequence: Singular Bernoulli convolutions are not only a Pisot phenomenon. Internal to fractal geometry.

154.why: Multiple ergodic averages converge almost everywhere for mixing maps; rests on two other unchecked release papers.
154.consequence: Pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages for mixing maps; depends on two other release papers.

155.why: Translational tiles that tile 3D space only non-periodically, the lowest possible dimension; Lean checks it.
155.consequence: Aperiodic translational tiles exist in 3D, the lowest possible dimension. Internal.

156.why: Borsuk's conjecture fails in dimension 9, down from 63 months earlier, by a topological route; Lean checks it.
156.consequence: Borsuk's conjecture fails from dimension 9; dimensions 4 to 8 stay open.

157.why: Claims to disprove Hadwiger's 1943 conjecture, graph minor theory's central problem; the disproof is unchecked, only a side bound is.
157.consequence: Would overturn graph minor theory's central conjecture. The safe, Lean-checked part is a linear bound on list coloring.

158.why: The plane cannot be colored with 5 colors so no two points 1 apart match; the answer is now 6 or 7. Lean checks it.
158.consequence: The plane needs 6 or 7 colors. Little follow-on beyond the problem.

159.why: Erdős's $5000 question: sets with divergent reciprocal sum contain long progressions; Lean checks the Erdős statement.
159.consequence: Progressions in any set with divergent reciprocal sum, plus quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds usable throughout additive combinatorics.

160.why: Two-color van der Waerden numbers grow faster than any exponential, answering Erdős; Lean checks the bound.
160.consequence: Van der Waerden numbers grow faster than exponential. Internal.

161.why: Counterexamples to Sidorenko's conjecture on bipartite pattern counts, long believed true; Lean checks it.
161.consequence: Ends the Sidorenko and forcing conjectures, which much of quasirandomness theory hoped to rest on.

162.why: Ryser's covering conjecture fails at large rank; no explicit example is given. Lean checks it.
162.consequence: Ryser's bound fails at large rank; small ranks stay open.

164.why: Any finite coloring of the integers has a set whose sums and products share one color, as Hindman asked; no Lean.
164.consequence: Sums and products together in one color. Internal to Ramsey theory.

165.why: Exact crossing numbers of complete and complete bipartite graphs, open 60-80 years, by short algebra; Lean checks both.
165.consequence: Exact crossing numbers of complete and complete bipartite graphs. Little follow-on beyond graph drawing.

166.why: Erdős distinct distances in every dimension 3 and up, to a constant factor; 103 pages weeks after a human 3D advance.
166.consequence: Distinct distances in higher dimensions settled up to constants. Internal.

167.why: First improvement on the 1984 n^{4/3} unit-distance bound, by a number-field trick; the gain is ineffective. Lean checks it.
167.consequence: A first improvement on the 1984 unit-distance bound, by an arithmetic method that may reach other incidence problems.

168.why: Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials depend only on the shape of the Bruhat interval, a 1980s conjecture; Lean checks it.
168.consequence: KL polynomials are determined by poset shape, a combinatorial handle on Schubert variety cohomology.

169.why: The graded Shareshian–Wachs refinement of Stanley–Stembridge e-positivity; the ungraded case was proved in 2024.
169.consequence: Graded e-positivity of chromatic quasisymmetric functions, relevant to Hessenberg varieties.

170.why: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, building on a 2026 human construction; Lean checks it.
170.consequence: Sharp log exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, building on a recent human construction.

171.why: Burr and Erdős's 1975 question: hypercubes have linear Ramsey numbers; a big jump in 172 unformalized pages.
171.consequence: Linear Ramsey numbers for hypercubes. Internal.

172.why: An algebraic criterion for which finite point sets are Euclidean Ramsey, a 50-year question; Lean checks it.
172.consequence: An algebraic classification of Ramsey configurations, not an algorithm.

173.why: Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture: some vertex has as many second as first out-neighbors; 15 Lean-checked pages.

174.why: Every k-edge-connected graph has a C/k-thin spanning tree, built deterministically; Lean checks it.
174.consequence: Deterministic thin trees, a structural tool from traveling-salesman approximation.

175.why: Talagrand's conjectures on rounding fractional expectation thresholds, in short papers; Lean checks two of three.
175.consequence: Talagrand's threshold conjectures become tools for locating thresholds of random structures.

176.why: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture: thresholds for spanning subgraphs are right to one log factor; Lean checks it.
176.consequence: Sharp thresholds for random graphs to contain large subgraphs.

177.why: The first bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every degree, from congruence coset complexes; Lean checks it.
177.consequence: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders, building blocks for topological overlap, quantum codes and PCPs.

178.why: A deterministic construction of non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs in every degree; existence was known. No Lean.
178.consequence: A deterministic construction of near-optimal expanders in every degree; existence was known.

179.why: Ryser's conjecture: no circulant Hadamard matrix beyond order 4, after 60 years of failed attempts; Lean checks it.
179.consequence: No circulant Hadamard matrices beyond order 4, ruling out even-length Barker sequences used in radar pulse compression.

180.why: Barnette's conjecture: cubic bipartite polyhedral graphs are Hamiltonian, in 11 pages; Lean checks the topological statement.
180.consequence: Settles the last piece of Tait's approach to the four-color theorem; non-constructive.

181.why: Erdős–Gallai: every graph splits into linearly many cycles and edges; Lean checks it.
181.consequence: Linear cycle decompositions for every graph. Internal.

182.why: Sets with no two elements a square apart have power-saving density bounds; Lean checks the square case.
182.consequence: Power-saving bounds for square-difference-free sets; the prime case leans on the release's quasi-RH.

183.why: Halving lines below Dey's 1998 n^{4/3} bound, by an ineffective amount; Lean checks it.
183.consequence: Breaks Dey's 1998 halving-lines bound by an ineffective amount.

184.why: K_r-free graphs get triangle-free-quality independence and coloring bounds, a 45-year target; Lean checks half.
184.consequence: Optimal coloring and independence bounds for K_r-free graphs, a 45-year target, with correspondence coloring included.

185.why: Counterexamples to the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection conjectures; the finitary one survives.
185.consequence: The unrestricted infinite matroid conjectures fail. Nothing follows beyond it.

186.why: Friedgut–Kalai's optimal 1/(log n)^2 threshold width for symmetric graph properties; Lean checks the graph case.
186.consequence: Optimal sharp-threshold width for symmetric graph properties.

187.why: Maker wins Snaky on the infinite grid in 21 moves, settling the last small polyomino; a Lean-checked certificate.
187.consequence: Settles one game. Nothing follows beyond it.

188.why: The exact number of edges left by random triangle removal, up to the constant; Lean checks it.
188.consequence: The exact constant for what random triangle removal leaves behind.

189.why: Cycle–clique Ramsey numbers for all remaining small cases; mostly known before. Lean checks the certificates.
189.consequence: Completes the last finitely many cases. Nothing follows beyond it.

190.why: Polynomial removal lemmas fail for ordered binary matrices, via one large pattern; Lean checks it.
190.consequence: Polynomial removal fails, limiting property testers for ordered matrices.

191.why: Heilbronn's triangle problem: the first power improvement on the 1982 lower bound; the exponent is tiny.
191.consequence: The first power improvement in Heilbronn's problem; the exponent is negligible.

192.why: Boolean functions can beat the square-root degree bound by any factor, against Gopalan–Servedio; Lean checks it.
192.consequence: Correlation with the input sum can beat the square root of degree. Internal to Boolean analysis.

193.why: Serre's 1965 positivity of intersection multiplicities, finishing the ramified case with perfectoid tools; unformalized.
193.consequence: Completes Serre's positivity in every characteristic, a cornerstone of intersection theory on regular schemes.

194.why: Lech's conjecture: multiplicity cannot drop along a flat map of local rings; Lean checks only a supporting lemma.
194.consequence: Settles Lech's question on multiplicities. Internal to commutative algebra.

195.why: A singular ring with no small Cohen–Macaulay module, in characteristic 0, against Hochster's conjecture; no Lean.
195.consequence: Removes one proposed route to several homological conjectures. Internal to commutative algebra.

196.why: Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture fails: a torsion-free group algebra over F2 with zero divisors. Lean checks it.
196.consequence: Ends a 70-year conjecture about group rings and forces the field to rethink Kaplansky's remaining conjectures (units fell in 2021).

197.why: A group algebra that is not directly finite, which yields the first known non-sofic group; Lean checks a torsion version.
197.consequence: A non-sofic group would settle Gromov's question and refute Gottschalk's surjunctivity, reshaping group theory and dynamics.

198.why: Bass's finitistic dimension conjecture fails for a fixed finite-dimensional algebra; Lean checks the bounds.
198.consequence: Bass's finitistic dimension conjecture is false, which removes a known route to the Nakayama conjecture.

199.why: Counterexamples to the Auslander–Reiten, Tachikawa and Nakayama conjectures on rigid modules; Lean checks the core.
199.consequence: Several rigidity conjectures in the representation theory of algebras are false, including Nakayama's.

200.why: Eisenbud–Green–Harris: lex-plus-powers ideals have extremal growth, in characteristic 0, with two proofs. No Lean.
200.consequence: A Macaulay-type theorem for complete intersections, with applications to Cayley–Bacharach.

201.why: Kurosh's problem: an algebraic division ring that is not locally finite; 45 unformalized pages.
201.consequence: Answers Kurosh's Burnside-type question for division rings. Internal to ring theory.

202.why: Alperin's weight conjecture blockwise, without the classification of finite simple groups; striking and unformalized.
202.consequence: Alperin's weight conjecture, and a classification-free method others could reuse in modular representation theory.

203.why: Donovan's conjecture: bounded defect gives finitely many block types; uses the classification. No Lean.
203.consequence: Finiteness of block types for bounded defect, a structural result many block-theory papers assume.

204.why: Tensor saturation for even spin groups, extending Knutson–Tao beyond type A; exceptional types remain. No Lean.
204.consequence: Saturation in one more Lie type. Internal.

205.why: Saxl's conjecture: the staircase representation's tensor square contains every irreducible; Lean checks it.
205.consequence: Settles Saxl's conjecture on Kronecker coefficients. Internal to algebraic combinatorics.

206.why: Not every finite lattice is a congruence lattice of a finite algebra, and the question is undecidable; Lean checks less.
206.consequence: Settles the finite lattice representation problem negatively and shows no algorithm can decide it.

207.why: The ℓ¹ Bass conjecture for all discrete groups, giving Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture in char 0; Lean checks the algebraic part.
207.consequence: Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture in characteristic 0 for every torsion-free group follows.

208.why: Finite symmetric tensor categories in characteristic p land in the Verlinde tower, as BEO conjectured; no Lean.
208.consequence: Classifies the targets of finite symmetric tensor categories in characteristic p. Internal.

209.why: Gersten's conjecture fails for ramified regular local rings; the unramified case stays open. No Lean.
209.consequence: Gersten's conjecture needs unramified hypotheses. Internal to algebraic K-theory.

210.why: Foulkes' plethysm conjecture for sixth powers only; the general conjecture stays open. Lean checks part.
210.consequence: One more case of Foulkes' conjecture. Nothing follows beyond it.

211.why: Random planar maps with critical FK clusters converge to Liouville quantum gravity, as physics predicts; 762 interlocking pages.
211.consequence: Puts the physics picture of random surfaces with critical clusters on rigorous ground, including random walk as Liouville Brownian motion.

212.why: Planar first-passage percolation has no doubly infinite fastest routes, a long-standing FPP question; Lean checks less.
212.consequence: Settles a central structural question of first-passage percolation and disordered systems in the plane.

213.why: No infinite cluster at criticality on every quasi-transitive graph; the famous Z^3 case was done first by others.
213.consequence: Completes the critical-percolation picture on symmetric graphs beyond the cases settled earlier.

214.why: Benjamini–Schramm: percolation on nonamenable graphs has a phase with infinitely many infinite clusters; Lean checks it.
214.consequence: Confirms the expected three-phase picture of percolation on nonamenable graphs.

215.why: Polyakov's prediction: 2D O(n) spin models with n≥3 have exponential decay at every temperature; Lean checks that part.
215.consequence: A rigorous mass gap for 2D spin models with n≥3, the lattice cousin of the Yang–Mills mass gap; the continuum limit papers build on it.

216.why: The fine BKT structure of the XY transition, including the exp(c/√t) correlation length; conditional pieces, no Lean.
216.consequence: Rigorous fine structure of the BKT transition for the cosine XY model.

217.why: Free-energy fluctuations of the SK spin glass at low temperature scale as n^{1/6}, as physicists predicted; no Lean.
217.consequence: Sharp fluctuation exponent for the SK model; the limit law is not identified.

218.why: Conformal invariance for Ising models with weak extra interactions or disorder; perturbative only.
218.consequence: Extends Ising conformal invariance beyond exactly solvable models, in the perturbative regime.

219.why: Random regular graphs of any fixed degree have GOE eigenvalue spacings, the sparse end of universality; no Lean.
219.consequence: Random-matrix statistics for sparse regular graphs, the long-missing sparse end of universality.

220.why: Random walks in random environments that escape in a direction must do so at positive speed; Lean checks it.
220.consequence: Escape forces speed for walks in random environments in d≥2, settling a central RWRE question.

221.why: The Mézard–Parisi formula for sparse spin glasses, in a restricted class of models; Lean checks it.
221.consequence: Rigorous replica-symmetry-breaking free energies for sparse spin glasses, in a restricted class.

222.why: Perceptron free energies and the jamming exponents predicted by full replica symmetry breaking.
222.consequence: Rigorous capacity formulas for the perceptron, the simplest neural-network capacity model, and its jamming exponents.

223.why: Conformal invariance of square-lattice random-cluster models for q in [1,4], including Cardy's formula; 602 unchecked pages.
223.consequence: Would extend Smirnov's conformal invariance to the square lattice for a whole range of q; among the largest claims in 2D statistical mechanics.

224.why: Cardy's formula for Voronoi percolation, averaged over the tessellation; no Lean.
224.consequence: Cardy's formula for a random-lattice model, averaged. Internal.

225.why: The six-vertex height function is a Gaussian free field throughout the balanced critical range; one paper, no Lean.
225.consequence: Confirms the Bethe-ansatz prediction for the six-vertex model's height fluctuations.

226.why: Loops from two overlaid domino tilings converge to CLE4, in half-plane Temperleyan domains; no Lean.
226.consequence: Upgrades double-dimer loop convergence to CLE4. Internal.

227.why: Glauber dynamics for the SK model mixes fast all the way to β=1, with the n^{2/3} critical slowdown; Lean checks parts.
227.consequence: Guarantees for Glauber sampling of spin glasses throughout the high-temperature phase.

228.why: A continuum gas with a radial pair potential that has a phase transition; the potential is engineered, not physical.
228.consequence: Shows continuum phase transitions can happen for a radial potential; says nothing about natural potentials.

229.why: Kesten–Stigum is the exact reconstruction threshold for 3 and 4 colors on trees; Lean checks only the easy direction.
229.consequence: Pins the community-detection threshold for 3-community block models.

230.why: The exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE curves, with an iterated-log correction; Lean checks the positivity half.
230.consequence: Settles Schramm's gauge question for SLE. Nothing follows beyond it.

231.why: The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID, answering Lyons; 19 Lean-checked pages.
231.consequence: Answers Lyons's question and covers all strongly Rayleigh invariant processes.

232.why: Random Lipschitz height functions on the triangular lattice converge to the Gaussian free field; no Lean.
232.consequence: Gaussian free field limit for Lipschitz heights. Internal.

233.why: The joint scaling limit of the critical Ashkin–Teller model; a narrow recent conjecture, no Lean.
233.consequence: Identifies one scaling limit. Nothing follows beyond it.

234.why: The free energy of rotation-invariant Ising spin glasses at every temperature; Lean checks it.
234.consequence: Free energies for spin glasses with non-Gaussian coupling structure, beyond the classic SK setting.

235.why: An alternative proof that random k-SAT thresholds converge, with variance and computability; existence is others' first.
235.consequence: Variance and computability of SAT thresholds; no threshold value is computed.

236.why: The free Ising state on a tree is a factor of IID exactly up to the Kesten–Stigum point; Lean checks it.
236.consequence: Sharp factor-of-IID threshold for tree Ising. Internal.

237.why: Self-avoiding walks on the honeycomb lattice spread like n^{3/4}, as physicists predicted; 1067 pages, the law itself unformalized.
237.consequence: Rigorous 2D self-avoiding walk exponent on one lattice; no scaling limit, not Z^2.

238.why: The Thorp shuffle mixes in O(d) rounds for 2^d cards, down from O(d^3); Lean checks a bound.
238.consequence: Fewer rounds of the Thorp shuffle needed for provable randomness, relevant to format-preserving encryption.

239.why: A random symmetric ±1 matrix is singular with probability about 2^{-n}, from equal rows; unformalized.
239.consequence: Sharp singularity probability for symmetric random sign matrices. Internal to random matrix theory.

240.why: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes, in ZFC; the main theorem is unformalized.
240.consequence: Brings Morley's categoricity theorem to abstract elementary classes, the main structural goal of that program.

241.why: The Turing degrees have no symmetry but the identity, finishing Slaman–Woodin in 10 pages; Lean checks it.
241.consequence: Settles the rigidity question for Turing degrees. Internal to computability theory.

242.why: Hilbert's tenth problem stays undecidable with at most one solution promised, via elliptic curves; Lean checks the core.
242.consequence: Hilbert's tenth problem stays undecidable under a unique-solution promise, with consequences for counting and complexity.

243.why: Choiceless polynomial time does not capture P, settling the Blass–Gurevich–Shelah conjecture; Lean checks it.
243.consequence: Removes the leading candidate logic for polynomial time; whether any logic captures P stays open.

244.why: The Partition Principle does not imply the Axiom of Choice, a question open since 1902; Lean checks the consistency.
244.consequence: Answers a 1902 question in set theory. Internal.

245.why: In every pure type system, weak normalization implies strong normalization (Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop); Lean checks it.
245.consequence: Settles a termination question about type systems underlying proof assistants; little follow-on.

246.why: Cannon's conjecture: hyperbolic groups with 2-sphere boundary are 3-manifold groups; 31 pages, Lean checks it.
246.consequence: Completes the 3-dimensional program in geometric group theory: groups recognized from their boundary.

247.why: An infinite finitely presented torsion group, the finitely presented Burnside question; Lean checks the periodic group.
247.consequence: A finitely presented infinite torsion group, a long-sought example. Internal to group theory.

248.why: Thompson's group F is not amenable, a famous 60-year-old question, in 13 pages; Lean checks it.
248.consequence: Settles a question many results were conditional on, and gives Dixmier counterexamples for F.

249.why: The Bestvina–Brady group that breaks Eilenberg–Ganea, so that one fails, not Whitehead; Lean checks it.
249.consequence: Identifies which of two conjectures fails for Bestvina–Brady groups; Whitehead stays open.

250.why: Boone–Higman: groups with solvable word problem embed in finitely presented simple groups; Lean checks it.
250.consequence: An algebraic characterization of groups with solvable word problem.

251.why: Dixmier's problem: every nonamenable group has a non-unitarizable representation; Lean checks it.
251.consequence: Unitarizability characterizes amenability. Internal to group theory and operator algebras.

252.why: A torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite, against Gromov's question; Lean checks it.
252.consequence: Hyperbolicity alone does not give residual finiteness; with Kapovich–Wise, a hyperbolic group with no finite quotients.

253.why: An infinite, finitely presented, simple and amenable group, from polygon exchanges; Lean checks it.
253.consequence: A new kind of simple group example. Internal.

254.why: The K(π,1) conjecture for all Artin groups, giving each a finite classifying space; Lean checks it.
254.consequence: Every Artin group gets a finite classifying space, torsion-freeness and computable cohomology.

255.why: Groups shaped like polycyclic groups are virtually polycyclic, by quasi-isometry; Lean checks it.
255.consequence: Quasi-isometric rigidity for polycyclic groups. Internal to geometric group theory.

256.why: Kervaire's conjecture: adding one generator and one relation never kills a group; Lean checks the core theorem.
256.consequence: Settles Kervaire's conjecture; Howie's stronger conjecture stays unformalized.

257.why: A hyperbolic group that acts geometrically on no CAT(0) space; Lean checks the main statement.
257.consequence: Hyperbolic groups need not be CAT(0); limits on geometric models.

258.why: Gersten's conjecture: one-relator groups without Baumslag–Solitar subgroups are hyperbolic; no Lean.
258.consequence: Hyperbolicity of one-relator groups, with virtual specialness as a companion.

259.why: Gaboriau's fixed-price question: a group whose actions have different costs; 27 unformalized pages.
259.consequence: Cost is not a group invariant. Internal to measured group theory.

260.why: The Penrose inequality for spacetimes: black holes carry at least Schwarzschild mass; 1,355 pages, with decay hypotheses.
260.consequence: A strong consistency check on cosmic censorship, with charged, rotating and anti-de Sitter versions.

261.why: Anderson model: electrons stay mobile under weak disorder in 3D and are trapped in 2D; uniform disorder law only, unchecked.
261.consequence: Rigorous metal–insulator behaviour for the Anderson model, the standard model of disordered conductors.

262.why: Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring inequalities for the remaining exponents; Lean checks the scalar case.
262.consequence: Sharp constants for 1D Lieb–Thirring inequalities. Internal to spectral theory.

263.why: The ionization conjecture: a nucleus of charge Z binds at most Z plus a constant electrons; the headline is unformalized.
263.consequence: Bounds how many electrons atoms can bind, matching experiment up to a constant.

264.why: Strong cosmic censorship, locally and generically, near two-ended Kerr black holes; not the full conjecture. No Lean.
264.consequence: Supports determinism in general relativity near Kerr; global SCC stays open.

265.why: Ground states of gapped 2D quantum systems obey an area law and have efficient tensor networks; 146 unformalized pages.
265.consequence: Explains rigorously why tensor-network methods work for gapped 2D quantum systems; not an efficient algorithm.

266.why: Dimension 6 has exactly 3 mutually unbiased bases; Lean checks at most 5, the rest uses floating-point certificates.
266.consequence: Optimal quantum tomography in dimension 6 cannot use a complete set of unbiased bases.

267.why: Bose–Einstein condensation for interacting bosons in the thermodynamic limit; Lean checks the ground-state version.
267.consequence: Rigorous Bose–Einstein condensation for interacting gases, a textbook phenomenon long unproved.

268.why: Haldane's 1983 prediction that spin-1 chains have an energy gap, via numerical certificates; 58 unformalized pages.
268.consequence: Rigorous footing for a cornerstone of topological phases of matter; the proven gap is tiny, existence only.

269.why: A uniform spectral gap for the Laughlin state of the fractional quantum Hall effect; Lean checks the core.
269.consequence: Incompressibility of the Laughlin state, which the fractional quantum Hall effect needs.

270.why: BFSS matrix model bound states at threshold, plus surprising positive-energy ones against the original paper; no Lean.
270.consequence: Makes index arguments in matrix theory rigorous; the positive-energy claim needs physicists' scrutiny.

271.why: The quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet magnetizes at low temperature in 3D, open for decades; Lean checks the theorem.
271.consequence: A rigorous proof that the textbook quantum model of a ferromagnet orders in 3D.

272.why: Applying a PPT channel twice can keep entanglement, refuting the PPT-squared conjecture; Lean checks it.
272.consequence: Settles a favourite quantum-information question; entanglement and secret key really differ.

273.why: The entropy photon-number inequality for beam splitters, a missing step for optical channel capacities; Lean checks it.
273.consequence: Settles several optical channel capacities that were waiting on this inequality.

274.why: Shallow quantum circuits with fan-in gates cannot compute parity, open 25 years; Lean checks it.
274.consequence: A clean limit on shallow quantum circuits, the quantum analogue of AC0 lower bounds.

275.why: Computing molecular ground-state energies is QMA-hard even with only hydrogen-like nuclei; Lean checks it.
275.consequence: Quantum chemistry's ground-state problem is hard in the worst case; says nothing about typical molecules.

276.why: The exact classical capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping qubit channel; Lean checks it.
276.consequence: Exact capacity for a realistic qubit noise model.

277.why: Concentration of rounds won in parallel-repeated entangled games, from known estimates; Lean checks a weaker rate.
277.consequence: Threshold bounds for entangled games from known estimates. Little follow-on.

278.why: A three-electron molecule whose density no non-interacting system reproduces, against a Kohn–Sham assumption; no Lean.
278.consequence: A foundational assumption of density functional theory fails in general, for one potential class.

279.why: Factoring exactly, with zero error, over a fixed finite quantum gate set in polynomial time; Lean checks it.
279.consequence: Removes error and continuous angles from Shor-type factoring; no practical speedup.

280.why: Unitary vertex operator algebras match conformal nets in the strongly rational case; Lean checks parts.
280.consequence: Links two axiomatizations of 2D chiral conformal field theory in the rational case.

281.why: QAOA gets arbitrarily close to the SK optimum in the large-size limit, with no depth bound.
281.consequence: QAOA's asymptotic power on SK; no depth or angle guidance for practice.

282.why: Scale symmetry gives local conformal symmetry in 4D QFT, but only inside a heavily axiomatized framework.
282.consequence: A result inside a strongly axiomatized framework; the physics question stays open.

283.why: A quantum circuit with a classical oracle implements any unitary to constant error in polynomial time; no Lean.
283.consequence: Relates quantum unitary complexity to classical complexity. Internal.

284.why: A nearly quartic gap between randomized and quantum query complexity, the most allowed; 19 unformalized pages.
284.consequence: Pins the largest quantum query speedup for total functions. Internal to query complexity.

285.why: Groups that break the Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky conjectures, via projections with irrational trace; 184 unchecked pages.
285.consequence: Would overturn a central prediction of noncommutative geometry: K-theory of group C*-algebras is not always computed by geometry.

286.why: Classifies finite-index relations between von Neumann algebras of higher-rank lattices; long, specialist, no Lean.
286.consequence: Rigidity for lattice von Neumann algebras. Internal to W*-rigidity.

287.why: The free group factors are all isomorphic, answering an 80-year-old question against expectation, in 23 pages; Lean checks it.
287.consequence: Ends the free group factor problem, with knock-on effects across free probability and von Neumann algebras.

288.why: Kadison's 1955 similarity problem: bounded representations of C*-algebras are similar to *-representations; Lean checks it.
288.consequence: Settles a 70-year problem; Kadison–Ringrose cohomology and Kadison–Kastler stability follow in this release.

289.why: Close von Neumann algebras are unitarily conjugate with a universal tolerance; it fails for separable C*-algebras.
289.consequence: Stability of von Neumann algebras under perturbation. Internal.

290.why: Connes' bicentralizer problem for type III_1 factors, in 35 pages; Lean checks only a supporting lemma.
290.consequence: Extends Haagerup's key step for hyperfinite factors to all type III_1 factors.

291.why: The comparison-implies-Z-stability step of the Toms–Winter conjecture, via uniform property Gamma; Lean checks part.
291.consequence: A key implication of the Toms–Winter conjecture, which drives the Elliott classification of C*-algebras.

292.why: Not every separable C*-algebra embeds in the ultrapower of O_2, answering Kirchberg; 14 Lean-checked pages.

293.why: An operator with no hyperinvariant subspace, also settling the transitive algebra problem; Lean checks it.
293.consequence: Settles the hyperinvariant subspace and transitive algebra problems; the invariant subspace problem stays open.

294.why: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture fails for a non-exact C*-algebra; 16 Lean-checked pages.
294.consequence: Quasitraces need not be traces, and stable finiteness is not preserved by tensor products.

295.why: Kadison–Ringrose: von Neumann algebras have vanishing Hochschild cohomology in themselves; Lean checks it.
295.consequence: Completes Kadison–Ringrose vanishing. Internal to operator algebras.

296.why: Every finite factor is generated by a single operator, Kadison's generator problem; Lean checks it.
296.consequence: Answers Kadison's generator problem for finite factors, with a free-entropy corollary.

297.why: Naimark's problem has a counterexample in plain ZFC; a human paper got there two days earlier. Lean checks it.
297.consequence: A ZFC answer to Naimark's problem, shared with a human paper.

298.why: The two notions of free entropy can disagree even when both are finite; Lean checks it.

299.why: A C*-algebra absorbs Jiang–Su exactly when its central sequence algebra has no character; Lean checks it.
299.consequence: A clean test for Z-stability, the regularity property behind C*-classification.

300.why: Strong-operator paving with optimal block count for every masa; specialist, unformalized.

301.why: After Razak–Jacelon stabilization, the trace cone classifies separable nuclear algebras; unformalized.
301.consequence: A classification result after stabilization. Internal.

302.why: Radius of comparison is exactly half the mean dimension for minimal Z-actions, via complex cobordism; no Lean.
302.consequence: Links dynamics and C*-regularity exactly. Internal.

303.why: The natural notions of pure infiniteness for C*-algebras coincide, giving O_∞ absorption; Lean checks it.
303.consequence: O_∞ absorption for nuclear algebras without simplicity, for the classification programme.

304.why: Hilbert–Smith: no group wilder than a Lie group acts faithfully on a manifold, via a new invariant; 46 unchecked pages.
304.consequence: Settles which groups can act faithfully on manifolds, completing a line from Hilbert's fifth problem.

305.why: The free group is not good for 4D disk embedding, a 40-year question behind Freedman's work; a novel, unchecked invariant.
305.consequence: Would show Freedman's 4D surgery methods cannot extend to all groups, reshaping 4-manifold topology; families 320 and 315 build on it.

306.why: Different Dehn surgeries on a knot never give the same oriented manifold, closing the last case by instanton counts.
306.consequence: Settles cosmetic surgery. Little follow-on beyond 3-manifold topology.

307.why: The coarse Novikov conjecture fails for a bounded-geometry space; Lean checks the reduced version, not the headline.
307.consequence: Limits the coarse Novikov approach to index theory on bounded-geometry spaces.

308.why: Smith–Toda complexes exist at every chromatic height for some large prime; whether V(4) exists at small primes stays open.
308.consequence: Existence of the basic finite building blocks of chromatic homotopy theory at all heights.

309.why: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime 3, the analogue of Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel; unformalized.
309.consequence: Settles which Kervaire invariant classes exist at the prime 3.

310.why: Quillen's conjecture on p-subgroup complexes, finishing the last p=2 cases after decades of reductions; no Lean.
310.consequence: Completes Quillen's conjecture in rational homology. Internal.

311.why: The Hovey–Strickland thick subcategory conjecture for K(n)-local spectra, via a reduction by others; no Lean.
311.consequence: Classifies thick subcategories in the K(n)-local category. Internal.

312.why: Grothendieck's homotopy hypothesis for one standard model of weak ∞-groupoids; Lean checks a key step.
312.consequence: Confirms Grothendieck's picture of spaces as weak ∞-groupoids for one model.

313.why: Each homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is finitely generated over the p-adic integers; no Lean.
313.consequence: Finite generation of the K(n)-local sphere's homotopy. Internal.

314.why: Sharp chromatic fixed-point loss for every p-group, by explicit finite spectra; no Lean.
314.consequence: Sharp chromatic Smith theory for p-groups. Internal.

315.why: The Singer conjecture in dimension 4: L2 homology of aspherical 4-manifolds sits in the middle; no Lean.
315.consequence: Settles Singer's conjecture in dimension 4. Internal.

316.why: Curtis's conjecture: only Hopf-invariant-one and Kervaire classes are spherical in QS^0; 37 unchecked pages.
316.consequence: Settles which homology classes of QS^0 are spherical. Internal to homotopy theory.

317.why: Strict n-categories model all homotopy types in every dimension, extending Thomason; Lean checks it.
317.consequence: Model-theoretic foundations for higher categories. Internal.

318.why: The chromatic splitting conjecture fails at height 3, while a weaker filtered form holds; 372 unformalized pages.
318.consequence: Revises a central conjecture about the structure of the stable homotopy groups of spheres.

319.why: An fp spectrum not finitely built from truncated Brown–Peterson spectra, against Hahn–Wilson; large primes only.
319.consequence: A counterexample to a finite-generation conjecture. Nothing follows beyond it.

320.why: Two non-homeomorphic aspherical 4-manifolds with the same fundamental group, so Borel fails in 4D; depends on family 305.
320.consequence: The Borel conjecture fails in dimension 4, if family 305 holds.

321.why: A counterexample to Wall's D(2) problem in 10 elementary pages; the reviewer re-derived the key computation.
321.consequence: Answers Wall's question, with implications for the relation between 2-complexes and group presentations.

322.why: Tingley's problem: an isometry between unit spheres of normed spaces extends linearly, in 12 pages; Lean checks it.
322.consequence: Settles Tingley's problem. Internal to Banach space geometry.

323.why: Banach's separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC; Lean checks the CH half.
323.consequence: The separable quotient question has no ZFC answer. Internal.

324.why: Separable Banach spaces can be Lipschitz equivalent without being linearly isomorphic, a central open question; Lean checks it.
324.consequence: Metric structure does not determine linear structure even for separable spaces, a basic limit for nonlinear Banach theory.

325.why: The complete (matrix-valued) Crouzeix conjecture; the scalar case was solved two months earlier. Lean checks it.
325.consequence: One similarity of condition number at most 2 controls functional calculus of any matrix, as operator theory wanted.

326.why: Finite cotype of a space and its dual forces K-convexity, under the approximation property; Lean checks it.
326.consequence: Entropy duality under cotype bounds follows. Internal to Banach spaces.

327.why: Only superreflexive Banach spaces have nontrivial Markov type, a Ribe-program question; Lean checks it.

328.why: Every nonexpansive self-map of a bounded closed convex set in a reflexive space has a fixed point; Lean checks it.
328.consequence: Reflexivity alone gives fixed points for nonexpansive maps, settling metric fixed point theory's central question.

329.why: Covering numbers are not stable under taking polars, refuting the metric-entropy duality conjecture; Lean checks it.
329.consequence: Entropy numbers of an operator and its adjoint can differ. Internal.

330.why: Uniformly discrete metric spaces whose free spaces lack bounded approximation, sharpening a recent human result.
330.consequence: A sharper counterexample after Smith. Nothing follows beyond it.

331.why: A reflexive space without AUC renorming that still avoids diamond embeddings, answering Baudier–Lancien.
331.consequence: Answers one problem from a list. Nothing follows beyond it.

332.why: ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype 2, so Hilbert-to-ℓ1 Lipschitz maps extend; 9 elementary, unformalized pages.
332.consequence: New Lipschitz extension results into ℓ1 via Ball's framework.

333.why: Every smooth surface metric is realized by a smooth immersed surface in R^4, one dimension below Gromov; Lean checks it.
333.consequence: Settles the dimension-4 case of isometric immersion for surfaces. Internal.

334.why: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in R^3, a classical open question; Lean checks it.
334.consequence: Settles the smooth local isometric embedding question in 3D. Internal.

335.why: Aspherical manifolds carry no positive scalar curvature metric in any dimension, Gromov's bound; 121 unformalized pages.
335.consequence: Positive scalar curvature obstructions for all aspherical manifolds, without spin or dimension limits; a new method others could reuse.

336.why: Positive scalar curvature makes a manifold thin in two directions, in every dimension; no Lean.
336.consequence: Settles Gromov's width and macroscopic-dimension conjectures for positive scalar curvature.

337.why: The Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric inequality in every dimension, known only up to 4 before; Lean checks the CAT(0) core.
337.consequence: Sharp isoperimetry for every nonpositively curved space, including singular ones.

338.why: Yau's uniformization: complete Kähler manifolds with positive bisectional curvature are C^n; no Lean.
338.consequence: Classifies positively curved noncompact Kähler manifolds, extending Frankel's picture.

339.why: Katok's entropy rigidity: volume and topological entropy agree only on locally symmetric spaces; no Lean.
339.consequence: Settles Katok's rigidity conjecture. Internal to dynamics on negatively curved manifolds.

340.why: An exact Lagrangian in a cotangent bundle that is not the zero section moved, refuting a central symplectic conjecture.
340.consequence: Would overturn a central belief of symplectic topology, that exact Lagrangians in cotangent bundles are trivial.

341.why: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture, building on the formalized tamed-to-compatible result; no Lean.
341.consequence: Hypersymplectic 4-manifolds are K3 or tori, a topological classification.

342.why: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible question for symplectic 4-manifolds, in 18 pages; Lean checks the main theorem.
342.consequence: Settles Donaldson's question and supplies estimates used by family 341.

343.why: In dimension 6 and up, symplectic ball packings are limited only by volume and two-ball non-squeezing; Lean checks it.
343.consequence: Symplectic packing in high dimensions has no hidden obstructions. Internal.

344.why: The metric Blaschke conjecture for the projective spaces, by volume comparison; no Lean.
344.consequence: Closes the metric Blaschke conjecture. Internal.

345.why: Every metric on a sphere of dimension 3 or more has infinitely many closed geodesics; a competing claim exists.
345.consequence: Settles the closed geodesics question for spheres, if the competing claim is resolved.

346.why: The singular set of a stationary varifold has codimension at least one, a 50-year GMT problem; 112 unformalized pages.
346.consequence: Removes a 50-year obstacle in regularity theory for weak minimal surfaces.

347.why: Counterexamples to strong topological versions of Arnold's fixed-point conjecture; the homological one stands.
347.consequence: Limits Arnold-type fixed-point bounds to the homological form.

348.why: Einstein 4-manifolds with positive sectional curvature are the round sphere or CP^2; Lean checks the classification.
