349.why: The Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres, in all dimensions; no Lean.
349.consequence: Identifies the second-smallest minimal hypersurfaces in spheres. Internal.

350.why: Yau's nodal-length conjecture holds for all smooth surfaces and fails in dimension 3 and up; Lean checks both.
350.consequence: Settles Yau's nodal question for surfaces and shows it fails for smooth metrics above.

351.why: In dimension 4, bounded scalar curvature prevents Ricci-flow singularities; in high dimensions it does not.
351.consequence: Clarifies when Ricci flow singularities can be detected by scalar curvature.

352.why: The Calabi flow can break down in finite time on CP^10, against Chen's conjecture; no Lean.
352.consequence: Ends Chen's conjecture on Calabi flow. Internal.

353.why: The affine Bernstein problem holds exactly in dimensions 3 to 9 and fails smoothly in 10; Lean checks dims 3-9.
353.consequence: Pins the dimension where affine Bernstein fails. Internal.

354.why: The least-area way to enclose volume in the cubic 3-torus: ball, tube, then slab; Lean checks it.
354.consequence: Settles one isoperimetric profile. Nothing follows beyond it.

355.why: Tangent flows at the first singularity of mean curvature flow of surfaces are unique; 100 hard pages, no Lean.
355.consequence: Uniqueness of blow-ups, a tool for analysing mean curvature flow singularities.

356.why: Gigli's curvature tensor bound characterizes Alexandrov spaces; Lean checks a key step.

357.why: Bi-Lipschitz charts at every regular point of an RCD space, a Cheeger–Colding question; no Lean.
357.consequence: Regular points of RCD spaces have true charts. Internal.

358.why: A 3-manifold with no conjugate points that admits no nonpositively curved metric; Lean checks it.
358.consequence: Separates two curvature conditions on 3-manifolds. Nothing follows beyond it.

359.why: A negatively pinched Kähler manifold not biholomorphic to a bounded domain; Lean checks it.
359.consequence: Pinched negative curvature does not force bounded domains. Internal.

360.why: Villani's conjecture: weak MTW curvature gives convex injectivity domains and regular transport; Lean checks it.
360.consequence: Regularity of optimal transport maps under weak MTW curvature.

361.why: Nonnegative Ricci curvature can increase the count of polynomial-growth harmonic functions, answering Yau negatively.

362.why: Collisionless plasmas governed by relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell stay smooth forever, open since 1986; Lean checks it.
362.consequence: Settles global existence for a basic plasma model, closing the Glassey–Strauss line of work.

363.why: Weak solutions of the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation are not determined by their data; Lean checks a weaker form.
363.consequence: Large-data weak Boltzmann theory cannot give uniqueness. Internal to kinetic theory.

364.why: Extends the 2024 derivation of Boltzmann from particles to smooth potentials, with Gaussian fluctuations; conditional.
364.consequence: Particle derivations of Boltzmann for realistic interactions, plus fluctuation laws.

365.why: The anisotropic Calderón problem in dimension 3 and up, with partial data; only a side result is Lean-checked.
365.consequence: Uniqueness for anisotropic impedance tomography and partial-data measurements; the mathematics of electrical imaging.

366.why: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture; a human proof appeared two days earlier, this is a second route.
366.consequence: A second proof that Mumford–Shah segmentation edges are tidy. Little new follow-on.

367.why: The first non-flat minimizing cone for the one-phase Bernoulli problem appears in dimension 7; the new half is unformalized.
367.consequence: Pins the critical dimension for singularities of the one-phase free boundary problem.

368.why: Sobolev homeomorphisms in 3D can be approximated by smooth injective maps, the Ball–Evans problem; no Lean.
368.consequence: Smooth injective approximation for 3D elasticity maps; numerical methods would need constructive versions.

369.why: The hot spots conjecture for smooth simply connected planar domains; polygons are not covered. Lean checks it.
369.consequence: Settles hot spots for smooth simply connected domains. Internal.

370.why: The Lane–Emden conjecture in every dimension, open for n≥5 for 30 years, in 20 pages; Lean checks it.
370.consequence: Liouville theorems that feed blow-up rates and a priori estimates across nonlinear elliptic PDE.

371.why: Stable blowup for a defocusing Schrödinger equation in dimension 12 at some large power; Lean checks it.
371.consequence: Blowup for defocusing NLS happens for an open set of data, not a thin one; specific dimension and power.

372.why: Boundary measurements determine smooth isotropic elastic moduli in 3D, after an earlier proof was retracted; Lean checks it.
372.consequence: Uniqueness for elastic inverse problems with full boundary data.

373.why: Three-electron Coulomb transport can have no optimal Monge map, for an engineered density; Lean checks it.
373.consequence: The Monge ansatz in strong-interaction DFT can fail. Engineered density, not physical.

374.why: Brenier maps move like the cube root of the target's movement, and that is sharp; Lean checks it.
374.consequence: Sharp stability rates for transport maps used in statistical estimation.

375.why: De Giorgi's 1978 conjecture in dimension 8, a jump from dimension 4 two days earlier; unformalized.
375.consequence: Flat phase-transition profiles up to dimension 8, completing the De Giorgi picture.

376.why: Forced Navier–Stokes flows on a torus can simulate any Turing machine; the forcing makes the PDE side easy.
376.consequence: A kinematic construction. Says nothing about unforced blowup.

377.why: Infinity-harmonic functions have Hölder continuous gradients in every dimension, open 20 years; no Lean.
377.consequence: Gradient regularity for best Lipschitz extensions. Internal.
